title: Walmart just changed its name
summary: Walmart officially changed its corporate name from Wal-Mart Stores Inc. to Walmart, effective February 1, 2018. This change is a strategic move to reflect its growing emphasis on e-commerce and digital presence, mirroring its rival Amazon. The company has expanded its online brands and digital sales, while also strengthening its grocery business to compete with Amazon's entry into the supermarket sector.

title: New Amazon venture not a threat, Cigna CEO tells investors
summary: Cigna CEO David Cordani stated that the new healthcare venture by Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JPMorgan Chase is not a threat to Cigna's business, reinforcing the dynamic nature of the industry. Cigna reported strong fourth-quarter earnings, beating Wall Street estimates for adjusted income from operations, and raised its 2018 outlook. The company also announced plans to return tax reform benefits to employees through increased wages and 401(k) contributions.

title: Amazon.com treats employees with rainforest workplace
summary: Amazon Inc. has opened a rainforest-like office space called The Spheres in Seattle, hoping its lush environment will inspire new ideas and collaboration among employees. The complex, housing 40,000 plants, is part of Amazon's continued expansion in Seattle and was opened by CEO Jeff Bezos using a voice command to Alexa. This investment underscores Amazon's commitment to its main campus while cities compete for its second headquarters, HQ2.

title: Alphabet Inc Releases Q4 2017 Results; Traffic Acquisition Costs Increase 33%, Net Income Shows Loss Due To One-Time $10 Billion Tax Charge
summary: Alphabet Inc. reported its Q4 2017 results, revealing a 33% increase in Traffic Acquisition Costs (TAC) and a net loss due to a one-time $10 billion tax charge from the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. Despite the tax impact, the company saw strong revenue growth, especially in its Cloud business which reached $1 billion in quarterly sales, and significant advancements in its 'Made by Google' hardware division, particularly with the Pixel 2. Alphabet also outlined plans for future growth in digital advertising, hardware, and AI, including an $8.6 billion share buyback and investment of repatriated earnings.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market is growing in Tampa Bay
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market is expanding its presence in the Tampa Bay region with a new confirmed location in South Tampa. This will be the sixth Sprouts in the Tampa Bay area and the second in Pinellas County, indicating continued growth for the grocery chain in the market.

title: Executive Compensation Filings Grow to Nearly 10,000 Words on Average
summary: A new Equilar report reveals that the average word count for the Compensation Discussion & Analysis (CD&A) sections in proxy statements grew to 9,490 words in 2017 due to companies' efforts to explain mandatory disclosures and align executive compensation with corporate strategy. While regulatory requirements are a factor, investor informational needs and evolving disclosure practices are also major drivers of this increase. The report highlights variations in disclosure practices, including the use of alternative pay graphs, and provides insights into the future of compensation disclosure.

title: HP Inc. Rounds Out Its Printer Voice Command Capabilities With Amazon Alexa
summary: HP Inc. has expanded its printer voice command capabilities to include Amazon Alexa, adding to its existing support for Google Home and Microsoft Cortana. This move follows HP's initial integration of voice commands into its printers last year and positions the company as a leader in bringing classic home components into the smart home ecosystem. The article suggests future enhancements could include printer troubleshooting via voice and integrated smart assistants directly in printers.

title: Is your technology flexible and relatable to customers?
summary: This article emphasizes the importance of using technology to enhance the customer experience in the automotive industry, rather than purely automating it. Paul Whitworth, senior vice president of DMS at Dealertrack, suggests that technology should be open and easy to use, enabling dealers to increase efficiency and improve the personal car-buying experience. The core message is to be where customers are (online) and use technology to build upon the winning formula of price, convenience, and trust.

title: AT&T tower move highlights Midtown's appeal as HQ2 site
summary: AT&T Inc.'s decision to vacate its 46-story Midtown tower in Atlanta underscores the area south of Technology Square as a strong contender for Amazon's $5 billion HQ2 project. The move, reported on January 30, highlights Midtown's appeal for major corporate investments. Related articles discuss AT&T's consolidation efforts and Atlanta's standing in the HQ2 competition.

title: “Internationalizing a concept like Urban Outfitters is three times the challenge”
summary: Stefan Laban, global head of URBN International, discusses the challenges and strategies for Urban Outfitters' global expansion. He highlights the complexity of internationalizing a multi-brand concept, the importance of flexibility, and the integration of online and offline retail experiences. Laban outlines plans for expansion in Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, emphasizing the need for localization and adaptation to different markets.

title: Never mind doubling down, Oracle is quadrupling cloud-based data centers
summary: Oracle announced plans to build 12 new cloud-based data centers, quadrupling its current total, to compete directly with cloud leaders like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft. This expansion is one of Oracle's largest infrastructure projects, aiming to boost its minimal market share in the cloud data-center space despite high capital expenses and existing market dominance by competitors.

title: 8 Catalysts That Are Moving Amazon Stock
summary: This article identifies eight catalysts influencing Amazon's stock performance. Bank of America analyst Justin Post highlights factors like the late stages of a bull market for tech stocks, the impact of tax reform, millennials' growing spending power, sustained e-commerce growth, the rise of streaming video, the disruptive potential of voice search (Alexa), and Amazon's leadership in AI. It also notes Walmart as a serious rival in the technology space.

title: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd Is Muddying Its Own Waters
summary: Alibaba (BABA) is diversifying into numerous ventures beyond its core e-commerce business, including furniture, groceries, and physical retail. While these projects offer potential, the author warns that such widespread diversification could lead to a lack of focus and inefficient management, echoing similar risks faced by Amazon, General Electric, and Procter & Gamble. The article questions whether these new initiatives will genuinely drive commerce or merely generate data and presence without clear monetization.

title: What’s Changed: 2018 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics
summary: Gartner's 2018 Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics highlights significant shifts in the market, driven by cloud adoption, Hadoop, and logical data warehouses. The report evaluates 22 providers, noting Oracle's continued leadership, Amazon Web Services' strong ascent, and Snowflake's remarkable improvement into the Challengers quadrant. Several new vendors entered the report, while others were removed, indicating a dynamic and evolving landscape for data management analytics.

title: Kroger fuels mealtime push with culinary innovation center
summary: Kroger has opened a 12,000 square foot Culinary Innovation Center in Cincinnati to develop recipes for its private brands, meal kits, and other mealtime offerings. This initiative is part of Kroger's Restock strategy to capture more "meal dollars" from consumers increasingly eating food away from home. The center will fuel innovation for Kroger's Prep + Pared meal kits and private brands like Simple Truth, aiming to boost sales and profit margins.

title: Amazon to pay $1.2 million in settlement over pesticide sales, U.S. says
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has agreed to pay a $1.2 million penalty to settle nearly 4,000 alleged violations of U.S. law related to the illegal sale of pesticides on its website. The company will also implement measures to monitor and remove illegal pesticide products from its platform. The violations stemmed from third-party sellers distributing products not licensed for sale in the United States, prompting Amazon to ban foreign sellers of pesticides and refund affected customers.

title: E-commerce firm Mercado Libre to open distribution centers in Mexico
summary: Mercado Libre, a Latin American e-commerce company, announced it will open two large distribution centers in Mexico with a $100 million investment, creating 3,000 jobs. This move aims to significantly improve logistics and speed up deliveries in Mexico's growing e-commerce market, where companies like Amazon are also heavily investing. The company views logistics as the most challenging and expensive aspect of e-commerce.

title: CNBC investigates public company that changed its name to Riot Blockchain and saw its shares rocket
summary: CNBC investigated Riot Blockchain, a company that changed its name from Bioptix and saw its stock soar on cryptocurrency hype. The article highlights several red flags, including insider selling, dilutive issuances, connections to controversial investor Barry Honig, and questionable acquisitions and annual meeting practices, raising concerns about the company's business practices and transparency.

title: The QVC Story: From TV to Multiplatform Brand
summary: QVC has successfully transitioned from a television-based shopping channel to a multiplatform brand by embracing e-commerce and digital engagement, notably after acquiring rival HSN and Zulily. The company differentiates itself by offering an entertaining shopping experience, focusing on product storytelling and live demonstrations, which has resonated with its customer base, including a lucrative demographic of millennial moms. This strategy, combined with their 30-year history of customer interaction data, has allowed QVC to thrive in a competitive retail landscape while retaining its unique brand identity.

title: Target to open a second Main Line store
summary: Target Corporation is planning to open a new small-format store in Devon, Pa., by the end of the year. This will be the retailer's second Main Line location, backfilling a space previously occupied by Kmart. The announcement follows news of another small-format Target store heading to Ardmore.

title: Technology ETFs Take the Lead After Market Correction
summary: Following a recent market correction, technology and sector-related ETFs are leading the recovery as investors return to growth-oriented trades. The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSEArca: XLK) outperformed the broader S&P 500, with internet and semiconductor-focused ETFs showing even stronger gains. Major tech companies like Amazon, Microsoft, and Netflix are significant drivers of the S&P 500's year-to-date advance.

title: Birds in a Cage: The Indian Green Card Backlog
summary: This article highlights the immense challenges faced by high-skilled Indian workers in the U.S. due to the green card backlog, often leaving them in immigration limbo for decades. It details the personal struggles of individuals like Vikas and Lokesh Marenayakanapalya with visa renewals, job mobility restrictions, and family uncertainty, advocating for reforms to the per-country cap that exacerbates these delays. Political and corporate voices also weigh in on the need for comprehensive immigration reform to retain talent and support the American tech sector.

title: Sprouts posts strong comps again as new stores excel
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market reported strong Q4 2017 net sales of $1.1 billion, a 16% increase, driven by a 4.6% comparable-store sales increase. The company plans to open thirty new stores in 2018, including its first in the mid-Atlantic region, and is expanding its private label offerings and online delivery services to compete in the evolving grocery market. Despite strong results, Sprouts faces investor skepticism due to intense competition from players like Whole Foods and Amazon.

title: Costco offers over $3.5M for St. Cloud site
summary: Costco proposes to build a 166,600-square-foot facility, including a warehouse and liquor store, in St. Cloud. The company is offering over $3.5 million for the site. This move reflects Costco's continued expansion efforts, following previous pitches for warehouses in Eagan and Northeast Minneapolis.

title: Popular goods sold through Amazon, Walmart and others are counterfeits: Government report
summary: A new government report reveals that federal investigators purchased numerous counterfeit popular products, including cosmetics and electronics, from third-party sellers on major e-commerce websites like Amazon and Walmart. The Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that many items, such as Urban Decay cosmetics and Yeti travel mugs, were fakes, posing potential health and safety risks to consumers. The report prompted concerns from lawmakers and industry groups, while the e-commerce companies involved stated their commitment to combating counterfeit goods.

title: Amazon buys startup Ring in $1B deal to run your home security
summary: Amazon.com Inc has agreed to acquire Ring, a video doorbell maker, for over $1 billion US, signaling a strategic move into home security and in-home package delivery. Analysts view this acquisition as a way for Amazon to enhance its Amazon Key service, facilitate grocery delivery adoption, and expand its smart home ecosystem. The deal positions Amazon to revolutionize home security, potentially impacting traditional security firms like ADT Inc.

title: Booking Holdings reveals $12.7B revenue, goes lukewarm on Airbnb threat
summary: Booking Holdings reported significant growth in 2017, with $12.7 billion in revenue and gross travel bookings of $81.2 billion. CEO Glenn Fogel addressed concerns about Airbnb, highlighting Booking.com's customer trust, integrated accommodation options, and a no-fee model for travelers as competitive advantages. The company plans to aggressively expand alternative accommodations and invest in in-destination experiences, while maintaining a strong relationship with Google and focusing on growth in China.

title: PepsiCo takes its vending brand Hello Goodness online to woo consumers who want healthier snacks
summary: PepsiCo is extending its "better-for-you" Hello Goodness vending brand to an online platform to capture the growing market for healthier snacks. The company is offering curated boxes of Hello Goodness products on Amazon, building on the success of its vending machines which saw significant revenue increases. This move is part of PepsiCo's broader e-commerce strategy to adapt to changing consumer shopping habits and drive impulse purchases online.

title: SailPoint to significantly grow Austin footprint with new office; More hiring in works
summary: SailPoint Technologies has secured a large lease for a new office building in Northwest Austin, allowing for significant growth and consolidation of its headquarters. The fast-growing software company, which recently went public, is expected to increase its hiring following this expansion. A rendering of their new headquarters is available, showcasing Merriman Anderson Architects' design.

title: Gartner Magic Quadrant: Who's Winning In The Data And Machine Learning Space
summary: This article analyzes Gartner's 2018 Magic Quadrant reports for Data Science and Machine-Learning Platforms and Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms. It highlights key leaders and departures in the BI space, such as Microsoft, Tableau, and Qliktech, and discusses Gartner's cautious stance on AI and Machine Learning adoption, emphasizing the importance of a data strategy. The author also notes discrepancies in vendor rankings between Gartner and other research firms like Forrester.
